title: Myth vs Fact: Pumping Your Brakes in an Emergency
hook: Stop pumping your brakes in an emergency!

script.narration: Stop pumping your brakes in an emergency!
script.visual_search: car braking suddenly on wet road

script.narration: Many drivers still believe pumping the brake pedal helps you stop faster on slippery roads.
script.visual_search: driver stepping on car brake pedal

script.narration: That's a dangerous myth. Modern vehicles feature ABS technology that automatically pulses your brakes up to twenty times per second. Pumping the pedal yourself actually overrides maximum ABS pressure and increases your stopping distance.
script.visual_search: dashboard abs warning light close up

script.narration: Like if this helped, follow for daily driving tips! Did your driver's ed teach this? Comment yes or no.

description:
Debunking a major driving myth: should you pump your brakes in an emergency? Learn how modern Anti-lock Braking Systems (ABS) work and why pumping the pedal can actually increase your stopping distance on slippery roads.

Subscribe to Learn in 60 Seconds for quick, actionable car tips and essential driving safety advice every single day.
